entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Bartolomeo Aicardi Visconti, a Roman Catholic prelate, served as the Bishop of Novara from 1429 until his death on May 7, 1457. His episcopate spanned a tumultuous period in 15th-century northern Italy, marked by the political dominance of the Duchy of Milan under the Visconti and later Sforza dynasties, and the ongoing struggles within the broader Catholic Church, including the Council of Basel. As Bishop of Novara, a strategically important city situated between Milan and the territories of Savoy, Aicardi Visconti navigated complex ecclesiastical duties alongside the demands of secular rulers, playing a role in maintaining the spiritual and administrative continuity of his diocese during a time of shifting allegiances and conflicts.

During his nearly three-decade tenure, Aicardi Visconti was responsible for the spiritual well-being of the Novarese diocese, overseeing clergy, administering sacraments, and managing church properties. His appointment in 1429 came at a time when the Visconti Dukes of Milan exerted considerable influence over episcopal nominations in their territories, ensuring the loyalty of key church officials. While specific details of his individual interventions are scarce, his long episcopate suggests a degree of administrative stability within the diocese, even as the region experienced the decline of Filippo Maria Visconti's rule and the brief Ambrosian Republic before the rise of Francesco Sforza.
